_comment: Scene for the navy and fleet panel. Renderer keys: 'windows' with 'at' (where the engine puts each top-level window on a 2560x1440 screen; leave it out to use the file's own position until it is measured with render_gui.py --verify), 'rows' and 'listRows' (sample rows per list), 'height', 'hide' and 'place' (what the code sizes, hides or moves in this state); 'samples' (texts for named text boxes). Harness keys: 'setup' (recipe steps from the clean state; see wiki/Game-Recipes.md), 'captures' (extra named captures with their own steps), 'expect' (widgets that must be visible in the capture: proof that the recipe brought the screen up), 'crop' (x, y, width, height cut out of a capture). 'manual' and 'checklist' are what is left for a human. 'rowsAcross' names the containers the code fills from left to right (the composition counters). A window with 'skip' is a row window listed for its 'hide' list only: another window draws it.

windows.name: naviesview_window
windows._note: The frame is transparent and 86 % of the screen high (1238 px) in vanilla and in the mod; 'height' here ends at the bottom bar line. The code puts one fleet card per selected fleet into detailed_fleet_box, the toolbar under the last card (168 px below the top with one fleet) and the task force cards under the toolbar.

windows.name: taskforce_view_entry
windows._note: The first task force card: 43 px below the toolbar. A card opened with Select shows alone, with its ships in ships_detailed (35 px per ship).

windows.name: fleet_view_header
windows._note: Drawn by naviesview_window as the row of detailed_fleet_box; listed here for its hide list only.
